'''Xiangyu Zhou''' ('''Zhou Xiangyu''', {{lang-zh|s=周向宇|p=Zhōu Xiàngyǔ}}, born March 1965) is a Chinese mathematician, specializing in [[several complex variables]] and [[complex geometry]]. He is known for his 1998 proof of the "extended future tube conjecture", which was an unsolved problem for almost forty years.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Zhou, Xiang-Yu |year=1998 |title=The extended future tube is a domain of holomorphy |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/1998/0005/0002/MRL-1998-0005-0002-a004.pdf |journal=Mathematical Research Letters |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=185–190 |doi=10.4310/MRL.1998.v5.n2.a4 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Zhou was born in March 1965 in [[Chenzhou]], [[Hunan]]. Zhou matriculated in 1981 at [[Xiangtan University]], where he graduated in 1985 with a bachelor's degree in mathematics. From 1985 to 1990 he studied at the Institute of Mathematics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], where he received an M.Sc. in 1988 and a Ph.D. in 1990. At Beijing's Institute of Mathematics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences he was from 1990 to 1992 an assistant professor and from 1992 to 1998 an associate professor and is since 1998 a full professor. During 1990 to 1992 he was on academic leave as a senior scientific member of the [[Steklov Mathematical Institute]], where he was awarded in 1998 a Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree.<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=周向宇 (with CV & list of "Representative Research Works")|website=中国科学院 (Chinese Academy of Sciences — math.ac.cn)|url=http://www.math.ac.cn/kyry/201407/t20140724_247885.html|access-date=2021-09-01|archive-date=2021-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210822193736/http://www.math.ac.cn/kyry/201407/t20140724_247885.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Zhou was from 2003 to 2012 the director of the Institute of Mathematics and is since 2008 the director of the Hua Loo-Keng Key Laboratory of Mathematics. From 2008 to 2011 he was the vice-chair of the [[Chinese Mathematical Society]].<ref name=homepage/>

Zhou was awarded in 1999 the First Class Prize of the Natural Science Award of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2001 the S.S. Chern Mathematics Prize of the Chinese Mathematical Society, and in 2004 the National Natural Science Award of China of the [[State Council of China]].<ref name=homepage/> In 2002 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Beijing.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Zhou, Xiangyu|title=Some results related to group actions in several complex variables|year=2003|eprint=math/0304337}}</ref> In 2013 he was elected an Academician by the Chinese Academy of Sciences<ref name=homepage/> and was a keynote speaker of the Abel Symposium.<ref>{{cite web|title=Abel Symposium 2013|url=https://abelsymposium.no/2013/files/Program-Abelsymposium-2013-2.pdf}}</ref>
